---
title: "Composition guide"
---

## Child widgets

Every layout widget accepts children either as a sequence or as a mapping. A
mapping is preferred for application-style notebooks because it gives each
child a stable key:

```python
from anylumino import TabPanel, TextWidget

tabs = TabPanel(
    {
        "status": TextWidget("Ready"),
        "logs": TextWidget("No events yet"),
    },
    titles={"status": "Status", "logs": "Logs"},
)
```

If `titles` is omitted for a mapping, the child keys are used as the titles.

## Accessing children

Layout widgets keep both a renderable widget and an owner object. This is useful
when a domain wrapper exposes a `.widget` view but also has methods that should
be called from Python.

```python
tabs = TabPanel({"price": price_chart})

tabs.get_widget("price")      # rendered child, usually price_chart.widget
tabs.get_owner("price")       # original wrapper object
tabs["price"]                 # same as get_owner("price")
tabs.call_owner("price", "fit")
```

## Mutating layouts after display

Children can be added, renamed, removed, and selected after the parent widget is
already displayed:

```python
tabs.add("chart-2", chart.widget, title="Chart 2", select=True)
tabs.rename_widget("chart-2", "Recent sample")
tabs.select_key("chart-2")
removed = tabs.remove_widget("chart-2")
```

## Scroll behavior

`HBox`, `VBox`, and `ScrollBox` can expose scrollbars inside notebook output.
The `scroll=True` convenience follows the natural axis:

```python
from anylumino import HBox, ScrollBox

wide = HBox(children, scroll=True, height=160)
vertical = ScrollBox(children, height=420)
```

For explicit overflow control:

```python
HBox(
    children,
    scroll_x=True,
    scroll_y=False,
    child_min_width=220,
)
```

## Resizing

Composed layouts are resizable by drag and drop by default. The resize handle is
shown in the bottom-right corner of the layout host.

```python
from anylumino import SplitPanel

SplitPanel({"left": controls, "right": chart}, sizes=[0.3, 0.7])
SplitPanel({"left": controls, "right": chart}, resizable=False)
```

`SplitPanel` uses Lumino split handles between child panes. The layout host
resize handle controls the overall notebook footprint.

## Actions and callbacks

Actions are plain dictionaries keyed by an `id`. The matching callback receives
the action id.

```python
from anylumino import Toolbar

toolbar = Toolbar(
    [
        {"id": "fit", "label": "Fit"},
        {"id": "marker", "label": "Marker"},
    ],
    callbacks={
        "fit": lambda _id: chart.fit(),
        "marker": lambda _id: chart.marker(text="Event"),
    },
)
```
